more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
more_info.overview: Sucrose esters of fatty acids is used as an emulsifier in food. Its technological role is to help oil and water remain mixed.
more_info.uses: EU permissions include milk-based drinks and similar products intended for young children. These permissions depend on the food category and its conditions of use.
more_info.daily_intake: 0-30 mg/kg body weight (JECFA, 1997). This is a combined limit for sucrose fatty-acid esters and sucroglycerides.
more_info.origin: Prepared by combining sucrose with suitable food fatty-acid derivatives, or recovered from sucroglycerides. This is a chemically processed sugar-and-fat ingredient.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: The fatty-acid feedstock is not specified as exclusively plant derived. Vegan, vegetarian, halal and kosher suitability cannot be established without the supplier identifying the raw material and processing.
more_info.side_effects:
The 2018 food-use exposure estimates exceeded the limit for several groups.
EFSA considered the estimates likely to overstate actual exposure.
